function.name: list_tasks
function.description: List active tasks, oldest first. Omit project_id to search all projects.

function.name: get_task
function.description: Fetch one task with its subtask roll-up and blocked/blocking flags.

function.name: create_task
function.description: Create a task. Omit project_id to file it in the General project.

function.name: update_task
function.description:
Partially update a task; only the fields present in `changes` are touched.

A parent's estimated_minutes is derived from its subtasks and cannot be set. Its
workflow_status may be set to open or in_progress while every subtask is still
open; done is reached only by completing the subtasks. A blocked task cannot be
marked done. Recurring tasks accept edit_scope "this" (default) or "future".

RepeatInterval.description:
A task recurrence cadence, e.g. ``{"unit": "week", "every": 2}``.

Both fields are always required (no defaults), so a partial payload is a 422
rather than a silently ``None`` cadence. ``every`` is bounded 1-12 to match
the natural-text UI (``daily`` … ``every 12 months``).
RepeatInterval.title: RepeatInterval

function.name: complete_task
function.description: Mark a task done. A recurring task spawns its next occurrence.

function.name: reopen_task
function.description: Reopen a done task (workflow_status back to open).

function.name: trash_task
function.description:
Move a task to the trash, together with all of its subtasks.

Undo with restore_task(task_id, restore_subtasks=True), which brings back
the same set. Plain restore_task(task_id) returns only this task and leaves
its subtasks in the trash.

function.name: restore_task
function.description:
Restore a trashed task (see list_trash for what is restorable).

Set restore_subtasks=True to also restore the subtasks that were trashed
together with this task — that is the exact undo of a trash_task call.
Subtasks the user had trashed separately beforehand stay in the trash.

function.name: list_dependencies
function.description: Both directions of a task's dependency graph: what it waits on (depends_on) and what waits on it (dependents).

function.name: add_dependency
function.description: Make task_id wait on depends_on_task_id: it is blocked until that task is done.

function.name: remove_dependency
function.description: Remove a dependency edge by its id (from list_dependencies); task_id must be its dependent.

function.name: skip_occurrence
function.description: Skip a recurring task's current occurrence (to trash, restorable) and return the next one.

function.name: stop_recurrence
function.description: Stop a recurring task from repeating; the current occurrence stays as a normal task.

function.name: list_projects
function.description: List active projects in display order.

function.name: get_project
function.description: Fetch one project.

function.name: create_project
function.description: Create a project.

function.name: update_project
function.description: Rename a project or edit its description; only fields present are touched.

function.name: close_project
function.description: Close a project: hidden from default lists, nothing deleted.

function.name: reopen_project
function.description: Reopen a closed project.

function.name: trash_project
function.description: Move a project and its tasks to the trash. Undo with restore_project.

function.name: restore_project
function.description: Restore a trashed project; restore_tasks also brings back the tasks trashed with it.

function.name: search
function.description: Full-text search over active projects and tasks (title, description).

function.name: get_focus_plan
function.description: Deterministic day plan: what to work on for `date` (default: today).

function.name: pin_focus_task
function.description:
Pin a task into the Focus plan for `date` (default: today) so it never lands in "Didn't fit".

With start_time (HH:MM) it becomes a fixed block at that time; without, it
joins the day ahead of the ranked work. Pinning an already pinned task moves
it. Undo with remove_focus_entry(entry_id).

function.name: add_focus_commitment
function.description:
Block fixed time in the Focus plan for something that is not a task, e.g. a 14:00 meeting.

The plan packs tasks around it. Undo with remove_focus_entry(entry_id).

function.name: reorder_focus_pins
function.description:
Reorder the pinned tasks in the Focus plan for `date` (default: today), first to last.

entry_ids are pin entry_ids from get_focus_plan; pins left out keep their
place. Commitments and pins at a fixed time keep their own times. Undo by
reordering back.

function.name: remove_focus_entry
function.description:
Unpin a task or drop a commitment from the Focus plan (entry_id from get_focus_plan).

Undo with restore_focus_entry(entry_id).

function.name: restore_focus_entry
function.description: Bring back a Focus pin or commitment removed with remove_focus_entry.

function.name: list_trash
function.description: Recently trashed projects and tasks — what restore_task/restore_project can bring back.

function.name: list_activity
function.description: A project's audit trail, newest first. actor is null for the user; agents stamp theirs (e.g. "agent:mcp", "agent:loop").

TaskDependencyRead.description:
A dependency edge plus the depended-on task's title/workflow state.

The denormalized title + workflow state let the client render the "Blocked"
indicator (depended-on task not yet ``done``) without a second round-trip.
TaskDependencyRead.title: TaskDependencyRead

TaskDependentRead.description:
A dependency edge plus the task waiting on this task.

This is the mirror of ``TaskDependencyRead`` for a task that is blocking
downstream work: it names each dependent task and exposes whether that task
is already done.
TaskDependentRead.title: TaskDependentRead

outputSchema.description:
Both directions of one task's dependency graph in a single payload.

The MCP ``list_dependencies`` tool returns this so an agent sees what the
task waits on and what waits on it in one call; the REST API keeps its two
separate endpoints.

mcp.name: search
mcp.description: Full-text search over active projects and tasks (title, description).

SearchResultItem.description:
One match, normalized across the searched entity types.

``title`` is the primary display line; ``subtitle`` is an optional secondary
line (e.g. a task's project name). ``project_id`` is populated for tasks so
the UI can route to the owning project when needed.

``workflow_status`` is populated only for the ``task`` kind (``None`` for
projects). It lets the command bar's ``/done`` action offer only
not-yet-done tasks; plain search ignores it.
SearchResultItem.title: SearchResultItem

outputSchema.description: Matches grouped by kind. Each group is independently capped by the service.
outputSchema.title: SearchResults

mcp.name: get_focus_plan
mcp.description: Deterministic day plan: what to work on for `date` (default: today).

BlockedTask.description: A task kept out of the schedule because a dependency is unfinished.
BlockedTask.title: BlockedTask

BlockingTask.description:
An unfinished dependency that is keeping a blocked task off the schedule.

Carries the blocker's title and workflow status so the UI can show *what* the
task is waiting on (and how close it is to done) without a second fetch per id.
BlockingTask.title: BlockingTask

CommitmentBlock.description: A fixed-time commitment that is not a task (a meeting), placed on the day.
CommitmentBlock.title: CommitmentBlock

CommitmentRepeatInterval.description:
A commitment series' cadence: the task shape plus an optional weekday set (#427).

``{"unit": "week", "every": 1, "days": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]}`` is a Mon-Fri
standup; ``every: 2`` with ``days`` is "every other week on those days".
``days`` is only meaningful with ``unit: "week"``; without it a weekly series
lands on its first day's weekday, as before. Task recurrence keeps the plain
``RepeatInterval``: this subclass is commitments-only.
CommitmentRepeatInterval.title: CommitmentRepeatInterval

DueSignal.description:
How a task's due date relates to the plan's target day.

Derived in the scheduler (no stored column): ``overdue`` is past, ``due_today``
is the target day, ``due_soon`` is within the look-ahead window, ``none`` has no
due date.
DueSignal.title: DueSignal

OverflowTask.description:
A schedulable task that did not fit in the available capacity.

Returned in ranked order so the UI shows the most important unscheduled work
first instead of hiding it.
OverflowTask.title: OverflowTask

ScheduledBlock.description: A task placed into a concrete time slot in the day's timeline.
ScheduledBlock.title: ScheduledBlock

SkippedCommitmentBlock.description:
A repeating commitment's occurrence that has been skipped for the day (#429).

Listed apart from ``FocusPlan.commitments`` so nothing reading the plan
mistakes it for time that is taken: it holds no time and blocks nothing.
``entry_id`` is the series; ``skip_entry_id`` is the skip row, and
``DELETE /focus/entries/{skip_entry_id}`` un-skips the occurrence (its undo
is ``POST /focus/entries/{skip_entry_id}/restore``).
SkippedCommitmentBlock.title: SkippedCommitmentBlock

outputSchema.description: The full deterministic plan for a single day.
outputSchema.title: FocusPlan

mcp.name: list_trash
mcp.description: Recently trashed projects and tasks — what restore_task/restore_project can bring back.

ProjectTrashRead.description:
A trashed project plus how many tasks would return if restored with it.

``archived_task_count`` is the set cascade-soft-deleted with the project (it
drives the restore confirm). ``purge_task_count`` is the wider set a purge
destroys — every trashed task the project still owns, including ones the user
trashed independently — so the irreversible confirm can't understate its scope
(BUG #189). Only used by the trash list, so the shared ``ProjectRead`` stays
unchanged.
ProjectTrashRead.title: ProjectTrashRead

RepeatInterval.description:
A task recurrence cadence, e.g. ``{"unit": "week", "every": 2}``.

Both fields are always required (no defaults), so a partial payload is a 422
rather than a silently ``None`` cadence. ``every`` is bounded 1-12 to match
the natural-text UI (``daily`` … ``every 12 months``).
RepeatInterval.title: RepeatInterval

outputSchema.description:
Recently soft-deleted rows across the user-facing tables (Sprint 7).

Powers the single /trash page — one fetch, restore via per-entity routes.
outputSchema.title: TrashRead
